title: Proof of the isosceles law: x = y ⟺ (4x − 2p)(4z − p) = 2p²
connection: 2/x + 1/z = 4/p ⟺ (4x − 2p)(4z − p) = 2p², so A = 4x − 2p ∈ {2, 2p, 2p²} (≡ 2 mod 4) and B = 4z − p ∈ {p², p, 1} must be ≡ −p (mod 4): impossible iff p ≡ 1 (4). The shape y = z gives (4x − p)(4z − 2p) = 2p² with the same conclusion. Hence isosceles solutions exist ⟺ p ≢ 1 (mod 4) (p odd prime) — confirming the data exactly.
why: A complete, elementary proof of an empirical fingerprint: the degenerate (isosceles) locus of the ES surface is obstructed exactly on the hard class by a mod-4 divisor condition — a miniature T1-type reciprocity obstruction; for general n it predicts failure ⟺ every prime factor of n is ≡ 1 (mod 4) — verified exactly for all 2 ≤ n ≤ 3000 (344 numbers, = A004613 minus 1).
first_step: Write it up as a lemma (the composite case follows from the same factorisation of 2n²); ask whether every certificate line has such a 'degenerate-locus' shadow.

title: Reorganise search: 'barrier-first' dataset of every approach × which step fails, as a public table
connection: Repo's barriers B1–B9 ↔ a public, structured negative-results database prevents others from repeating.
why: Negative results are under-published; a curated table is a community service and clarifies what remains.
first_step: Export FRONTIER §3/§4 barrier map as a CSV with (approach, step, barrier, reference) and render as a web page.

title: ESC(p) as a certificate count at primes — calibrate ESC(p)/log²p
connection: ESC(p) (words with some coordinate in 4ℤ ∪ (8ℤ−p)) is existence-equivalent to ES at primes per CONTEXT, but it is a count of certificates, not a lower bound for the number of solutions (ESC(5) = 6 > U(5) = 2); its residual follows χ_p with α ≈ −0.24 (R²-gain 0.31).
why: If ESC(p)/log²p is bounded below empirically with a cleaner constant than U, it is the better target count for lower-bound heuristics.
first_step: Compute min_{p ∈ [X,2X]} ESC(p)/log²p up to 3·10⁶ and compare its stability to U(p)'s.

title: Weak del Pezzo of degree 3 from the nodal ES cubic: Weyl-group orbits of the 9 lines
connection: The minimal resolution of the closure is a weak del Pezzo surface of degree 3 whose (−2)-curves form a root system. The Weyl group of the complement acts on lines/conic bundles. GEOMETRY_ES records 9 rational lines.
why: The lattice-theoretic structure (Pic ≅ I_{1,6}, roots) organises all conic fibrations, i.e. all 'Type I/II-like' families, in one Weyl orbit picture.
first_step: Compute the root system of the nodes and the orbit structure of conic classes; list the conic fibrations defined over ℚ and match them to known certificate types.

title: Symmetric coordinates
connection: Use s1=x+y+z, s2=xy+xz+yz, s3=xyz and the relation 4s3=ps2 to connect ES to integer-root cubic polynomials.
why: The cubic viewpoint keeps all denominator permutations together and exposes discriminant constraints.
first_step: Search small integer s1,s2 satisfying integral roots of T³−s1T²+s2T−ps2/4.

title: Parameterized complexity by factor count
connection: Treat the number of distinct auxiliary prime factors or modulus structure as an algorithmic parameter.
why: Subset-product search may be tractable in a parameter even when the integer itself is large.
first_step: Derive running-time bounds for residue selection in terms of factor count and group invariant factors.

title: Adelic interpolation: p-adic solution families at 2 and p glued with archimedean windows
connection: ES at p = existence of a global point; locally at 2, p, ∞ the solution sets are open sets (2-adic patterns, Type I/II at p, size windows at ∞). Strong approximation fails (it's a cubic surface integral-point problem), but measuring the adelic volume of the 'window' gives the expected count.
why: The adelic window volume times the global density should reproduce log²p; mismatch identifies missing local factors.
first_step: Compute the product of local densities at 2, p, ∞ (window) and small primes for the ES integral-point count; compare with Elsholtz–Tao's average.

title: Hirzebruch–Jung / Dedekind sums reciprocity as a forcing identity
connection: Dedekind-sum reciprocity s(a,c)+s(c,a) = (a/c + c/a + 1/(ac))/12 − 1/4 relates HJ continued fractions of a/c and c/a; ES certificates have HJ/CF data (DEDEKIND_ES).
why: Exact reciprocity laws are the only kind of 'charge identity' that work pointwise; the repo found the Dedekind–HJ discharging charge χ-blind.
first_step: Look for a twisted Dedekind sum (with a character mod 4C) whose reciprocity law is χ-sensitive and test on ES certificates.

title: Kummer-style 'regular' primes for ES: an invariant κ(p) that makes ES provable
connection: Kummer proved FLT for regular primes (p ∤ class number) long before Wiles. Look for an arithmetic invariant κ(p) (class number of ℚ(√−p), 2-rank/4-rank, parity of the fundamental unit norm of ℚ(√p), ℓ(p)) such that ES (or a sub-route) is provable for all p with κ(p) in some set, giving an infinite every-p family.
why: Partial every-p theorems on natural infinite sets of Mordell-hard primes do not yet exist; Kummer's theorem is the historical model.
first_step: Correlate (★)/ES₅ counts with κ(p) candidates for p ≤ 10⁸ and look for an invariant whose small/large values guarantee many certificates.

title: Shift two unit fractions while preserving exactness
connection: The Egyptian-fraction rewriting operator in arXiv:2003.13229 and ES F12/F14/F27: exact reciprocal decompositions admit local transformations while positivity/parity constrain the result.
why: A local rewrite may move a representation into the denominator congruence classes required by ES without changing the sum.
first_step: Read the operator identity and apply it to a two-term portion of a known three-term ES identity; check whether it preserves three terms and positivity.

title: Counterfactual feature interventions
connection: Alter one arithmetic feature in synthetic parameter data while holding the exact algebraic model fixed where possible.
why: This helps distinguish genuine mechanisms from correlated labels in observational prime data.
first_step: Within one residue-compatible family, vary a single auxiliary prime factor and measure the resulting target-residue change.

title: Catalog: Goldbach binary: 2n = p + q
connection: Goldbach binary: 2n = p + q ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ n / log² n (power). Obstruction: none (parity barrier for sieves). Status: open; almost all (Chudakov, van der Corput, Estermann 1938); verified to 4·10^18. Mechanism: circle method for almost all; parity problem blocks pointwise.
why: Power count yet open: shows count size alone never suffices; ES is far thinner but has multiplicative (divisor) structure.
first_step: Contrast the exceptional-set exponents: Goldbach exceptions ≪ x^{1−δ} vs ES exceptions ≪ x·exp(−c log^{2/3} x); ask why ES's is weaker.

title: Quadratic reciprocity obstructions in parametrised identities
connection: Reciprocity-limited parametrisations share F08, F09, F29: a natural family fails on a quadratic-residue locus.
why: Alternative reciprocity symbols or multiple parameters may cover complementary loci.
first_step: For each known ES family, record its Legendre-symbol condition and test whether two families have complementary failure sets.

title: −1 ∈ subgroup ⇔ even order: a parity reformulation of the e-slice event
connection: For prime e, −1 ∈ H ⊂ 𝔽_e^× iff |H| is even; the e-slice needs −1 in the quotient set Q (not the generated subgroup), but −1 ∈ ⟨Q⟩ is a necessary condition expressed via 2-adic valuations of multiplicative orders.
why: Converts part of the ES event into 2-adic order statistics of primes modulo e, a theme in Artin-type problems (OAI 029, Moree).
first_step: For hard primes, compute for each e-slice whether −1 ∈ ⟨factors⟩ and whether −1 ∈ Q; quantify how often the necessary condition holds but Q misses −1.
refs: Moree, Artin's primitive root conjecture – a survey, arXiv:math/0412262

title: Character orthogonality and real-character main terms
connection: Quadratic-form representation counts split into genus characters and an analytic remainder (F20,F31); ES likewise has a real-character main term in its sum over moduli (F20).
why: The decomposition may help isolate whether a genus-style positive main term can dominate the ES error for each prime, not merely on average.
first_step: For each C in R(p), expand the residue indicator using characters modulo 4C and explicitly separate principal, real, and nonreal characters for p≡1 mod 4.

title: Sparsity index: why binary Goldbach is stuck and ES is worse
connection: Binary Goldbach has a main term n/log²n among ~n terms and never got pointwise; ES has main term ≍ log²p among ≍ p log p 'trial events' (PARITY_AUDIT trial form).
why: Quantifies how far ES is from any problem ever upgraded; directs search to reformulations with denser events (fewer trials, larger main term).
first_step: Define sparsity = log(main term)/log(#trials) for each ES reformulation (★, b=1, ES₅, e-slice, I3 words) and tabulate; look for the least sparse one.
